thread:
sasha: Heads-up: nodepool deploys started failing with 403 for some CI jobs hitting GPU pools. Not widespread yet but saw 8 failures in the last hour. :warning:
ben: Logs? stack traces?
sasha: kube-apiserver audit shows "forbidden: User ... cannot create deployments.apps in namespace gpu-prod". SA was `ci-runner@namespace`. Also saw KMS decrypt errors for envelope tokens from the token service around the same time.
ryan: :eyes: Could be the new namespace-scoped policy rollout. I pushed a role split yesterday to limit cluster-adminish bindings. Did we accidentally revoke create on deployments for that SA?
ben: Checking RBAC: `kubectl get rolebinding -n gpu-prod` shows a `ci-runner-deploy` RoleBinding bound to ClusterRole/ci-runner-full from last week.
sec-bot: Audit alert: 2310000500 - clusterrolebinding-change - user=sasha created ClusterRoleBinding/ci-runner-full -> triggered.
sasha: I did create that binding earlier during the load test, thought it was temporary, I must have forgotten to delete it. Then I replaced it with a namespaced Role in the PR later but looks like the change didn't roll to the gpu-prod nodepool due to controller sync error.
ryan: That explains KMS decrypt errors — the controller that wraps ephemeral SA tokens uses KMS key access, and it's scoped to nodepool-keystore project. If binding is stale, token path mismatches and the decrypt fails.
ben: Repro steps I used:
```
kubectl -n gpu-prod auth can-i create deployments --as=system:serviceaccount:ci:ci-runner
# returns "no"
kubectl -n gpu-prod get rolebinding ci-runner-deploy -o yaml
```
sasha: Short-term mitigation: re-create the namespaced RoleBinding pointing to `role/ci-runner-narrow` in gpu-prod and restart token-proxy on nodepool-gpu controller to force token refresh.
devops-oncall: I'll restart token-proxy on nodepool-gpu now (rolling restart, safe window). ETA 3m.
ryan: Also patch Gatekeeper constraint to allow the `token-proxy` controller to reconcile; current constraint flagged the controller's create on ClusterRoleBinding as violation and auto-removed it. We should whitelist controllers via `metadata.annotations['controller-role']` instead of ClusterRole exceptions.
sec-bot: Suggested urgency: high. Create follow-up ticket for least-priv refactor and audit log correlation: https://redwood.internal/ops/SEC-1247
ben: Proposed RoleBinding YAML for immediate apply:
```
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: ci-runner-deploy
  namespace: gpu-prod
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: ci-runner
  namespace: ci
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: ci-runner-narrow
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```
sasha: Applying that now in gpu-prod.
ben: Confirmed `auth can-i` now returns yes for create deployments.
devops-oncall: token-proxy restart completed. KMS decrypt errors cleared per logs.
ryan: Follow-ups: 1) Add e2e to catch broken controller sync (PR in 48h). 2) Run RBAC audit across nodepools and flag any ClusterRoleBindings referencing ci namespaces. 3) Rotate KMS key used for token envelopes (scheduled) and ensure key ACLs are explicit.
sec-bot: Action items added to SEC-1247. tagging: @sasha @ben @ryan @devops-oncall :white_check_mark:
sasha: Sorry for the churn — lesson: don't leave temporary ClusterRoleBindings lying around. I'll also add a TTL cleanup in the controller.
ben: We should also add a postmortem note: root cause = stale ClusterRoleBinding + gatekeeper constraint interplay + controller sync bug.
ryan: I'll draft a short postmortem and link the RBAC diff and audit findings.
sasha: Thanks everyone. Closing thread once postmortem linked. :pray:
